config.title: Default Props

intro.title: Default Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple Vue component that displays user profile information. You'll learn how to use default props to provide fallback values when parent components don't pass specific data. The core concept is component communication through props with safety nets for missing data. You'll work with Vue's props system, JavaScript objects, and the defineProps compiler macro. This will help you create more robust components that handle missing data gracefully.
intro.usecase: Default props are essential for creating reusable components that work reliably even when parent components don't provide all expected data. In real-world Vue applications, you'll see this pattern in dashboard widgets that need sensible fallback values when data isn't available, form input components that should display placeholder text when no label is provided, and UI card components that need default styling when no custom classes are passed. This ensures your components never break unexpectedly and provide consistent user experiences across different parts of your application.

objectives: Configure a Vue component with default property values
Apply default props to components that receive no parent data
Initialize component properties with fallback values when props are undefined
Manipulate component behavior by overriding default props with parent-provided values
Construct reusable components that maintain consistent behavior across different usage contexts
Render components with predictable outputs using default property configurations
Integrate default props with Vue's prop validation system for robust component design

steps.title: Import Vue and defineProps
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the defineProps function from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and defineProps from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to Vue's defineProps function for working with component props.
successCriteria: Vue and defineProps are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineProps from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and defineProps from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'ProductCard' using defineComponent. Return an empty template for now.
steps.hint: Use defineComponent to define your component. The component should be a function that returns an object with a template property.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and defineProps from 'vue'

// Create the ProductCard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ProductCard component is defined with defineComponent and returns an empty template.
successCriteria: ProductCard component is created using defineComponent and has a template property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using defineComponent and returning a template.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a component named ProductCard using defineComponent with an empty template.

steps.title: Define props with types
steps.instruction: Inside the ProductCard component, use defineProps to define props with their expected types: name (string), price (number), and inStock (boolean).
steps.hint: Use defineProps with an object where each key is a prop name and the value is its type (e.g., String, Number, Boolean).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has typed props defined, ready to receive data from a parent component.
successCriteria: defineProps is called with an object containing name: String, price: Number, and inStock: Boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined all three props with their correct types: name (String), price (Number), and inStock (Boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the setup function, use defineProps to define the three props with their types as specified.

steps.title: Add default values to props
steps.instruction: Import the withDefaults helper from 'vue' to set default values for your props.
steps.hint: Add withDefaults to your import statement alongside defineProps.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing withDefaults
import { defineProps, withDefaults } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The withDefaults helper is imported and ready to be used for setting default prop values.
successCriteria: withDefaults is imported from 'vue' in the import statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported withDefaults from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import withDefaults from 'vue' to set default prop values.

steps.title: Create template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your ProductCard component that returns a div wrapper element.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, you can add a template section with the <template> tag. The template should contain the HTML structure your component will render.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template property with a div element as the root wrapper.
successCriteria: The ProductCard component has a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a template property with a div element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Remember to add a template property to your component with a div element as the root wrapper.

steps.title: Display prop values in template
steps.instruction: Inside the template string, add a heading that displays the product name prop value using Vue interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display the prop value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a prop value in template template: '

{{ productName }}

'
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the product name prop value when rendered.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation syntax displaying the product name prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct interpolation syntax {{ }} to display the prop value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the product name prop. Add interpolation syntax to show the prop value.

steps.title: Create a child component
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named 'ProductPrice' that will accept props.
steps.hint: Define a new constant variable called 'ProductPrice' and assign it an object with a 'setup' method that returns an empty object and an empty 'template' string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new Vue component named ProductPrice is created with a setup method and template property.
successCriteria: The code contains a 'ProductPrice' component object with 'setup' and 'template' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a complete Vue component object with both 'setup' and 'template' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductPrice component isn't properly defined. Remember to create a constant variable named 'ProductPrice' with a Vue component object structure.

steps.title: Define props with defaults in child
steps.instruction: Inside the ProductPrice component's setup function, use defineProps with withDefaults to define a 'price' prop with a default value of 0.
steps.hint: Use withDefaults(defineProps({...}), {...}) to provide default values for props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductPrice component will have a 'price' prop with a default value of 0 defined using withDefaults.
successCriteria: ProductPrice component uses withDefaults(defineProps({ price: Number }), { price: 0 }) in its setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using withDefaults with defineProps and providing the correct default value for the price prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductPrice component doesn't have the correct prop definition with defaults. Try using withDefaults(defineProps({ price: Number }), { price: 0 }).

steps.title: Use child component in parent
steps.instruction: Inside the ProductCard component's template, add the ProductPrice component as a child element.
steps.hint: Use the component name as a custom HTML tag in the template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductCard component's template now contains the ProductPrice component as a child element.
successCriteria: ProductPrice is included as a child element inside ProductCard's template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure ProductPrice is included as a child element inside ProductCard's template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductPrice component should be added as a child element inside ProductCard's template string.

steps.title: Pass props to child component
steps.instruction: In the ProductCard component's template, add the ProductPrice component and pass the 'price' prop value to it.
steps.hint: Use the ProductPrice component like a regular HTML element with a prop binding.
steps.analogousExample:
// Passing a prop to a child component
<ChildComponent :someProp="parentValue" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component will pass a prop value to the child component, which will use its default value if no prop is provided.
successCriteria: ProductPrice component is used in ProductCard's template with a bound 'price' prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the ProductPrice component in the template and binding the 'price' prop correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductPrice component isn't being used in the ProductCard template with a bound 'price' prop. Try adding it to the template section.
